title.point: God takes care of us, and we should give Him the credit.

lastWeekReview.title: Deborah and Barak—Defeating Jabin
bullets: The children of Israel were being mistreated by King JABIN, but no one would take the lead to fight and no one would follow a leader.
Everyone just did what was right in their OWN eyes, so they stayed stuck in a miserable situation.
When all the men had failed God, He raised up a WOMAN, Deborah, to be a judge — she did what was right in GOD’s eyes.
Deborah knew she couldn’t lead the army herself, so she called BARAK, the right man to lead the 10,000.
Barak would only go if Deborah went with him — with the proper leaders in place, the men followed in EXCELLENT order!
The enemy had 900 iron chariots, but JEHOVAH fought for Israel and threw Sisera’s whole army into confusion — the land had rest 40 years.
lastWeekReview.discussion: This week, was there a moment when you followed a proper leader — a parent, teacher, or serving one — instead of doing your own thing? How did it go, and what happened?
lastWeekReview.verseQuote: “The way of the fool is right in his own eyes, / But a wise man listens to counsel.” — Proverbs 12:15

kidsContent.text: After Deborah and Barak, Israel went back to their old ways and stopped listening to God. So God put them in the hand of their enemy, the MIDIANITES, for seven long years — until Israel finally cried out to Him.
God chose Gideon to lead only 300 men against a huge enemy. The camp of Midian was so big it looked like a swarm of LOCUSTS! It might have seemed impossible.

To strengthen Gideon, God sent him to the edge of the camp, where he overheard a man tell of a DREAM — a round barley loaf rolled in and knocked the tent flat. It meant God had given the enemy into Gideon’s hand! Gideon worshipped God and grew bold.

Gideon split the 300 into groups. Each man held a TRUMPET and a torch hidden inside a jar. At Gideon’s signal they blew the trumpets, smashed the jars so the torches blazed out, and shouted, “A sword for Jehovah and for Gideon!” The enemy panicked, drew their swords, and God made them fight one another!
🌟 Gideon had only 300 men, but JEHOVAH won the battle. God does not need a large number — He needs those who obey and take His way!

image.caption: Gideon’s 300 with trumpets, torches, and jars rout Midian

kidsContent.text: After the victory, the people were so happy they wanted to make Gideon their RULER. But Gideon said no! He knew he had not won the battle — GOD had. So he gave God the credit and worshipped Him.
God does not need great numbers or strong armies. He only needs those who OBEY Him and take His way — just like Gideon and his little band of 300.

God takes care of us too, even when we don’t realize it. (One storyteller drove a worn-out old van on a long road trip; only afterward did the mechanic find it had almost no oil and bad brakes — God had kept them safe the whole way!)
🌟 When God takes care of us and helps us do something, let’s be like Gideon — obey Him, trust Him, and give Him the credit!

lesson.practicePoint: This week, when something goes well or you finish something hard, don’t grab the credit for yourself — remember that God took care of you and helped you. Thank Him out loud and give God the credit!

memoryVerse.text: …I will not rule over you… Jehovah will rule over you.
memoryVerse.application: When the people wanted to make Gideon their ruler, he would not take the honor. He knew GOD had won the battle, so he gave God the credit. God is the One who takes care of us, so we can give God the credit too!

parts.text: Materials: Toy trumpets or paper horns, “torches” (yellow paper flames or flashlights), and “jars” (paper cups or bags to hide the light), plus a leader to be Gideon.

Setup: The children are Gideon’s 300 men, spread out in a big circle around a pretend “camp of Midian” in the center. Remind them: watch Gideon and do EXACTLY what he does — he gave very few instructions ahead of time!
Round 1 — Keep It Hidden: Everyone tiptoes into place with the torch hidden inside the jar. No noise, no light! The enemy must not know we are coming.

Round 2 — Watch Gideon: When “Gideon” blows his trumpet and lifts his torch, EVERYONE does the same at the same moment — blow the trumpets, uncover the torches, and shout together, “A sword for Jehovah and for Gideon!”
Round 3 — God Wins the Battle: The “enemy” (leaders acting confused) spins around in a panic and “falls.” The kids see that they never had to swing a sword — God won the battle for them!
📖 Connection: Gideon’s 300 only obeyed and gave God the credit — Jehovah did the fighting. God takes care of us and wins for us, so we give Him the credit!

rolePlayScript.text: Scene: Night on a hillside above the huge camp of Midian. Gideon and his helper Purah crouch in the dark; the 300 men wait behind them with trumpets, torches, and jars.
Israel had done evil, so God let the Midianites oppress them for seven years. When the people finally cried out, God chose Gideon and just 300 men to fight an enemy as many as the locusts.
Gideon, look at all those tents! There are thousands and thousands of them. And there are only 300 of us. How can we possibly win?
I felt afraid too, Purah. But listen — Jehovah told me to creep to the edge of their camp and hear what they are saying.
So they crept close in the dark. Inside a tent, a Midianite soldier was telling his friend about a strange dream.
I dreamed a round loaf of barley bread came tumbling into our camp, struck a tent, and flattened it to the ground!
That can only mean one thing — it is the sword of Gideon! God has given our whole camp into his hand!
Did you hear that, Purah? Even our enemies know God will win! I worship You, Jehovah. Now I am bold — it is time!
Gideon divided the 300 into groups. Each man took a trumpet in one hand and a torch hidden inside a clay jar in the other. Then Gideon said, “Watch me — and do exactly what I do.”
Now — blow the trumpets! Smash the jars! Let the torches blaze! Shout it out: “A sword for Jehovah and for Gideon!”
A sword for Jehovah and for Gideon!
Trumpets blast, jars shatter, torches flare all around the camp. The Midianites wake in terror, swords flashing in the dark.
We’re surrounded! Lights and trumpets everywhere! Grab your sword — attack, attack!

But God threw the whole camp into confusion, and the enemy swung their swords at one another. Gideon’s 300 never had to fight — Jehovah won the battle! Afterward the people wanted to make Gideon their king.
Gideon, you saved us! Rule over us — you and your sons after you. You should be our king!
No, I will not rule over you. I did not win this battle — Jehovah did. He is the One who takes care of us. Give the credit to God!
God takes care of us and fights for us — so we give Him the credit!

description.text: Setup: Split into “groups of 100” like Gideon’s 300. Give each team a toy trumpet, a paper “torch,” and a cup or bag for a “jar” at a start line, with a pretend camp of Midian at the far end.

Rules: One at a time, each runner tiptoes to the camp keeping the torch hidden in the jar (no light showing!). At the camp they “smash the jar,” raise the torch, blow the trumpet once, and shout, “A sword for Jehovah and for Gideon!”
Out: If your torch shows before you reach the camp, do 5 jumping jacks and start that turn over — the enemy must not see us coming!
Win: The team most together — every runner obeying the same signal — wins, not just the fastest. Gideon’s men all watched him and moved as one.
📖 Connection: The 300 only obeyed and made noise — GOD won the battle. When God takes care of us, we give Him the credit!
Materials: Toy trumpets or paper horns, paper torches, cups or bags for jars, open space
Setup: Everyone lines up behind one leader who plays “Gideon.” The rest are his small band of 300.
Rules: Gideon gives NO instructions ahead of time — the band must watch closely and copy his every move exactly: march, crouch low, raise a torch, blow a trumpet, freeze.
Out of Step: Anyone who moves before Gideon, or does their own move, sits out one round — Gideon’s men had to pay careful attention and do just as he did.
Twist: Rotate the “Gideon” each round so everyone practices watching a leader and obeying right away.
📖 Connection: God does not need a large number — just those who obey and take His way. A little band that obeys God can win!
Materials: Open space, optional toy trumpet and paper torch
Choose one leader to be “Gideon.” Everyone else is one of the 300, spread out in a wide circle around a marked “camp of Midian” in the middle of the field.
Goal: Keeping your “torch” (a flashlight or yellow cloth) hidden, quietly move into your place around the camp. Nobody reveals their light until Gideon gives the signal.
Signal: When Gideon raises his torch and “blows the trumpet,” EVERYONE at once lifts their torch, makes their trumpet sound, and shouts, “A sword for Jehovah and for Gideon!”
Finish: Gather in the center and thank God that He fought the whole battle — the 300 only had to obey. Give God the credit!
Materials: Flashlights or yellow cloths, a center marker, open outdoor space

outdoor.tip: 🎺 The lesson is trust and credit: God takes care of us and wins the battles we could never win. Help the kids feel that a small group that simply obeys God can see Him do great things — then give the credit back to Him, like Gideon did.
